sections.heading: What Causes Window Seals to Fail?
sections.body: Insulated glass units are designed with two or three panes of glass separated by a sealed air or gas-filled space. Over time, the seals that hold this system together can break down due to repeated temperature fluctuations, age, moisture infiltration, or physical stress. In Falls Church, where seasonal temperature swings are common, this kind of wear is especially frequent. Once the seal is compromised, outside air and humidity enter the space between the panes, causing that characteristic cloudy or foggy appearance. Beyond the cosmetic issue, a broken seal reduces the insulating efficiency of your window, meaning your heating and cooling systems have to work harder. Catching the problem early and scheduling professional broken window seal repair in Falls Church VA can prevent further glass damage and help maintain comfortable interior temperatures year-round.

sections.heading: How the Broken Seal Repair Process Works
sections.body: The repair process begins with a thorough inspection of the affected windows to confirm that seal failure is the root cause of the fogging or condensation. In some cases, surface condensation can mimic the appearance of a broken seal, so accurate diagnosis matters. Once a failed insulated glass unit is confirmed, we carefully remove the glass from the frame, taking care not to damage surrounding materials. A new insulated glass unit — matched to the original specifications — is then fabricated or sourced and installed with fresh sealant and glazing materials. We clean the frame, inspect the surrounding area for any contributing issues, and test the finished installation before we leave. Our goal is a repair that looks clean, performs well, and lasts.

faq.q: Can a broken window seal be repaired without replacing the entire window?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. When only the seal and the insulated glass unit have failed — and the frame itself is in good condition — we can replace just the glass unit rather than the entire window assembly. This is typically more cost-effective and less disruptive than a full window replacement.

faq.q: How do I know if my window seal is broken?
faq.a: The most common sign is persistent fogging, cloudiness, or visible moisture between the panes of glass. This condensation cannot be wiped away because it is trapped inside the sealed unit. You may also notice distortion or streaking on the glass that doesn't clean off. If you see any of these signs, it's a good idea to have the window inspected by a professional.
